property_summary: After calling SetMinSum(0) but before calling Initialized, the reference version sets MinSum to 0, so a deposit of 1 wei by alice then a Collect(0) call will succeed (since balances[alice] >= MinSum becomes 1 >= 0). The second version fails to set MinSum (the statement is missing), so MinSum remains default 0 nonetheless, but the critical difference is that the reference's SetMinSum actually assigns, while the buggy one does nothing – however both leave MinSum=0. The actual divergence: In the reference, subsequent initialization (Initialized) is possible and Collect works; in the buggy version, SetMinSum can be called again (since it never sets intitalized) but more importantly the key divergence is that after SetMinSum, the reference has actually stored the value, while the buggy version still has MinSum=0 (same as default), so the property we test is that calling SetMinSum(10) actually changes MinSum. After calling SetMinSum(10) before Initialized, MinSum should be 10 in reference, but stays 0 in buggy version.
